en: Harmalah ibn Yahya ibn 'Abdullah ibn Harmalah ibn 'Imran at-Tujibi narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed me: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah, who informed him that 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar informed him that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab set out with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) in a group of people towards Ibn Sayyad, until he found him playing with boys near the fortress of Banu Maghalah, and Ibn Sayyad was at that time approaching puberty. He did not notice until the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) struck him on the back with his hand, then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to Ibn Sayyad: 'Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?' Ibn Sayyad looked at him and said: 'I testify that you are the messenger of the unlettered.' Then Ibn Sayyad said to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): 'Do you testify that I am the messenger of Allah?' But the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) rejected him and said: 'I believe in Allah and in His messengers.' Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'What do you see?' Ibn Sayyad said: 'There comes to me a truthful one and a liar.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'The matter has become confused to you.' Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'I have concealed something for you.' Ibn Sayyad said: 'It is ad-Dukh.' So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'Be off with you! You will never exceed your station!' Thereupon 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: 'Leave me, O Messenger of Allah, to strike his neck!' But the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to him: 'If he is he, you will not be given power over him; and if he is not he, there is no good for you in killing him.' And Salim ibn 'Abdullah said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar saying: After that, the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and Ubayy ibn Ka'b al-Ansari set out towards the date palms where Ibn Sayyad was. When the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) entered the date palms, he began shielding himself behind the trunks of the date palms, seeking to hear something from Ibn Sayyad before Ibn Sayyad could see him. The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) saw him lying upon a bed in a velvet cloak of his, murmuring unintelligibly from within it. But the mother of Ibn Sayyad saw the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) while he was shielding himself behind the date palm trunks, so she said to Ibn Sayyad: 'O Saf'—and that was Ibn Sayyad's name—'Here is Muhammad!' Thereupon Ibn Sayyad jumped up, so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'If she had left him alone, he would have made it clear.' Salim said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar said: Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) stood up among the people and praised Allah with what He is worthy of, then mentioned the Dajjal and said: 'Indeed, I warn you of him; there has been no prophet except that he warned his people of him. Nuh certainly warned his people of him, but I will say to you concerning him a statement that no prophet has ever said to his people: know that he is one-eyed, and that Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is not one-eyed.' Ibn Shihab said: 'Umar ibn Thabit al-Ansari informed me that some companions of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said on the day he warned the people of the Dajjal: 'Indeed, written between his eyes is Kafir, which whoever despises his deeds will read—or every believer will read.' And he said: 'Know that none of you will ever see his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, until he dies.'
